doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

title: Lead sheets, fake books and 'Barcelona' jam sessions
summary: He writes lead sheets for publishing; none of his tunes are in fake books, though 'Barcelona' is played at jam sessions.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How do you write out your tunes if you want to publish them? And how much of them gets written out? Because I know sometimes guitars uses tablature, but if you wanted to write a lead sheet —
Yeah you write a lead sheet with the melody and you write it with the changes above it and that’s really good enough for the publishing part of it, for the Library of Congress it’s good enough, yeah.
I see. Did any of your tunes ever show up in the many fake books now on the market? © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
Gee and if they did you probably could get like, you know, a check for 25 cents or something.

Yeah I think maybe you’re over-estimating the amount from the fake book. Yeah. I would love to have this tune — you know what? I met a guy in Dallas one time, he said whenever there was a jam session guys would play “Barcelona.” So that’s pretty nice. It’s a logical tune, it’s a smart tune, and the changes are not — they’re logical. The harmonies — it feels good to play. I’m not just saying that for myself, it just feels good to play. I would enjoy playing it even if I didn’t write it.
